title: MSHTrans: Multi-Scale Hypergraph Transformer with Time-Series Decomposition for Temporal Anomaly Detection

problem.claim: Temporal anomaly detection requires monitoring temporal data across diverse domains.

gap.claim: Existing unsupervised reconstruction-based anomaly detection approaches insufficiently explore complex short- and long-term inter-timestamp dependencies and lack integrated joint learning of short-term patterns and long-term temporal characteristics.

contributions.claim: MSHTrans uses hypergraphs to model multi-order temporal dependencies.
The framework combines multi-scale downsampling, fine- and coarse-grained representations, and trainable hypergraph neural networks for adaptive inter-timestamp relationship learning.
The framework integrates time series decomposition to extract periodic and trend components from multi-granular features for long-term dependency modeling.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors explicitly present MSHTrans as a novel multi-scale hypergraph transformer for temporal anomaly detection.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that MSHTrans outperforms state-of-the-art competitors by an average of 8.21% without point adjustment and 3.52% with point adjustment.

narrative_sequence.summary: Temporal anomaly detection has attracted research attention because of increasing temporal data monitoring needs.
Existing unsupervised reconstruction-based models inadequately handle complex short- and long-term temporal dependencies and do not jointly learn both dependency scales.
MSHTrans applies hypergraphs to model multi-order temporal dependencies.
Multi-scale representations, adaptive hypergraph learning, and time series decomposition capture complementary fine-grained, coarse-grained, periodic, and trend information.
The integrated model reconstructs time series for anomaly detection, with reported average improvements over state-of-the-art competitors under two point-adjustment settings.
